messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: SLO breach detected in eu-west-1 streaming tier — p99 latency > 2.5s for 5m, p95 ~ 420ms. Auto-mitigation: prefetch throttle enabled. See /incidents/1748500000
Maria K.: I'm on call. Observing a large spike in tail latency and a surge of paging (evictions) across cache shard group a-*. Impacting streaming sessions and some generation requests. Customers reporting slow responses. :frowning:
Devin L.: digging into logs now. Early signal: a config change pushed ~1748496000 that bumped prefix-hash salt and reduced cache hit rate on certain namespaces. Looks correlated with a surge of coldlookups -> paging.
Sanjay R.: can you point to the rollout? I rolled out a small prefix-salt tweak yesterday but A/B was limited to canary. Did canary finish? ReleaseBot: Deployment 2026-03-10T08:00Z: prefix-salting v3 -> 50% rollout started. Canary passed. Rollout to 50% at 1748494800.
Devin L.: interesting — traffic patterns changed and the new salt expanded keyspace, causing a lot of prefix churn. Cache hitrate for model-embed-v2 dropped from 0.78 to 0.22 on shards pfx-12/13. Paging reads up 6x.
Ophelia S.: Support: three customers opened high-priority tickets citing >5s responses and timeouts. One customer (acct:acme-corp) observed failures in batch embeddings. We should notify them of mitigation steps asap.
Maria K.: Mitigation plan: 1) Pause rollout (if still running) 2) Roll back salt to previous value for affected namespaces or route traffic to fallback model variant 3) Temporarily increase in-memory cache allocation for pfx-12/13 4) Re-enable aggressive warmup for hot prefixes 5) Throttle background prefetch to reduce eviction churn
Sanjay R.: I can pause the rollout and revert the salt on a couple of nodes. But full rollback needs DB migration steps — risky. Alternative: add temporary deterministic alias mapping for hot prefixes to previous hash.
Devin L.: checking metric graphs: p99 peaked at 4.8s at 1748500200, p95 at 620ms. Paging bytes/sec at the time peaked ~3.2GB/s. Eviction rate shot up from 120/s to 2.5k/s. KV backend latencies saturated.
Maria K.: Prioritize customer impact: which regions/models are worst? Devin?
Devin L.: eu-west-1 is worst, then us-east-1. Affected models: model-chat-light, model-embed-v2. Traffic skew: a few high-traffic customers hit the new salt boundary that redistributed keys.
Ophelia S.: I'm drafting a customer note to affected accounts. Will warn of degraded latency and that we're rolling mitigation. Also asking for any on-prem proxies they might be using that could amplify retries.
Sanjay R.: Actioning: reverting prefix salt on routing layer for canary cohorts (pfx-12/13) now. Command:

```bash
# revert alias mapping
infractl routing alias set --namespace model-embed-v2 --salt previous --scope pfx-12,pfx-13
```

Expect ~30s to propagate per region.
Devin L.: I've also increased cache quota on pfx-12/13 via autoscale override: +30% RAM to those shards. Doing that now.
Maria K.: Also switching prefetch mode from aggressive->conservative to reduce churn (Devin please). That should lower eviction rate but might increase cold fetches briefly.
Devin L.: done: prefetch config updated: prefetch.window=100 -> 25; prefetch.concurrency=8 -> 2. Confirming.
ReleaseBot: Rollout paused: prefix-salting v3 at 50% -> paused at 1748500302 by ReleaseBot via API request from Maria K.
Devin L.: After revert + cache bump + prefetch throttle, p99 dropped to ~1.9s at 1748500600 and trending down. p95 back to 360ms. Eviction rate down to ~400/s.
Ophelia S.: Customer note v1 posted to support queue; PMs alerted. Will send targeted update to Acme and two others. :email:
Maria K.: Good. Next steps: 1) Full rollback assessment for salt change (can we make it safe?) 2) Long-term: add canary traffic pattern tests and monitor keyspace distribution before rollout 3) Improve alerting to correlate cache hitrate drop to prefix config change
Sanjay R.: For the rollback safety: need a small DB migration window or implement alias mapping more broadly. I'll prepare a runbook for alias-based rollback that avoids DB changes.
Devin L.: Also adding a synthetic test to nightly job that simulates skewed customer traffic across salt variants. Will add to the onboarding checklist for prefix-hash changes.
Maria K.: Ops timeline: Keep this thread updated. If p99 stays <2s for 15m, we'll move to monitoring-only. If any customer reports timeouts, escalate to incident bridge.
Ophelia S.: Noted. I've flagged Acme as P0 and set the SLA coordinator to reach out.
Devin L.: Quicklogs from affected node (pfx-12):

```
2026-03-10T08:03:12Z cache miss key=abc123 prefix=pfx-12 backend_fetch_ms=1340
2026-03-10T08:03:12Z eviction key=oldkey reason=mem_pressure
2026-03-10T08:03:13Z kv_read timeout=5000 err=timeout
```

Shows backend latency amplified by paging.
Maria K.: Thanks. If anything regresses, ping @channel and we'll open a bridge. Great work on fast mitigation. :thumbsup:
Devin L.: Follow-ups I'll file: incident doc, root-cause draft, and automated canary tests. Assigning to myself and Sanjay.
Sanjay R.: I'll draft the alias rollback runbook and coordinate with infra for a safer full rollback path.
Ophelia S.: Customer comms sent to affected list; waiting for replies.
incident-bot: RESOLVED: SLO breach cleared in eu-west-1. p99 < 1.8s sustained for 20m. Incident status -> monitoring. Incident ticket: INC-1748500000.
